children: franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection last week. Notably, the Michigan-based operator runs 314 Wendy’s restaurants across 15 states. The expectation is that restaurants will remain open and employee wages and benefits will continue during the restructuring.

Meritage sought a court-supervised restructuring to repair its balance sheet after sustained declines in sales and profitability. It had already shut at least 60 underperforming Wendy’s locations late last year and also adjusted or dropped breakfast service at certain locations to improve unit economics. In 2025, Meritage saw revenue fall about 7.6% to $618M and swung to a loss of over $32M. Revenue then fell another 14% in the first half of 2026, and Meritage reported a $23 million loss for that period.

As part of its filing, Meritage attributed the distress to weak traffic and sales across the Wendy’s system, aggressive value promotions that pressured margins, high labor and operating expenses, and sharply higher beef prices.
For investors, the bankruptcy filing is another sign of pressure on Wendy’s franchise economics during a broader brand turnaround.

title: A major Wendy's franchisee filed for bankruptcy
